chunks: Saʿd, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wearing a sword in salat (prayer) while it had fur and al-kaymukht on it. He said: “There is no harm, so long as it is not known to be carrion.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: And salat (prayer) is not permissible in the skins of the other impure beasts, such as the dog, the pig, the fox, the hare, and whatever resembles that; and it is not purified by tanning.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْأَنْجَاسِ: impure things, ritually unclean substances or animals
key_terms.الْفِرَاءُ: fur or pelts attached to the sword
key_terms.الْكَيْمُخْتُ: a type of treated leather material
key_terms.تَقْلِيدِ السَّيْفِ: wearing or carrying the sword suspended on oneself
key_terms.جُلُودِ: skins or hides used as material
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: carrion; an animal not slaughtered according to the law

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear a sword with fur or leather in salat (prayer), and are impure animal skins purified by tanning?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of carrying or wearing a sword in salat (prayer) when it contains fur or treated leather, permitting it so long as it is not known to be from carrion. It also states that salat (prayer) is not valid in the skins of impure animals such as the dog and pig, and that tanning does not purify such skins.
